chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever assists a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will relieve him of seventy-three distresses: one in this world and seventy-two during the Great Distress.' He added: 'Where people are preoccupied with themselves.'

key_terms.كُرَبِهِ الْعُظْمَى: The Great Distress (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the spiritual reciprocity of aiding a believer, promising relief from seventy-three tribulations—thirty-three in this world and forty on the Day of Resurrection. The 'Great Distress' (Kurbat al-Uzma) specifically alludes to the moment of individual accountability when humanity is preoccupied with its own fate, highlighting the unique value of intercessory support during peak anxiety. This reflects the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity (Ta'awun) as a means of divine mercy.
